# Connection

> Connection lets AI clients use approved external services without receiving the user's provider credentials.

## Install in Codex

Connection is a remote Streamable HTTP MCP server. When a user asks you to install Connection in Codex, explain the commands before running them. Installation and login require the user's explicit participation.

```bash
codex mcp add connection --url __CONNECTION_ORIGIN__/mcp
codex mcp login connection --scopes mcp --oauth-client-registration dcr
```

The login command opens Connection's OAuth flow. The user signs in to Connection in the browser. Never ask the user to paste an LDAP password, Connection access token, or provider credential into chat or Codex configuration.

Installing and logging in do not grant access to GitHub, Jira, Confluence, or other providers. The user must connect a provider account and explicitly approve the Codex grant in Connection before provider actions become available. Company approval is off by default for existing and new Providers; users connect their own accounts directly unless an administrator enables approval for that Provider. When enabled, obtain valid company eligibility first. Follow the current Connections page; do not assume missing access always requires company approval. Shared-account eligibility is separate.

## Public URLs

- Installation guide: __CONNECTION_ORIGIN__/connection
- Connection console: __CONNECTION_ORIGIN__/connection/connections
- MCP endpoint: __CONNECTION_ORIGIN__/mcp

Do not infer additional endpoints, credentials, identities, grants, or permissions from this file.

## Newly published Provider capabilities

New capabilities require explicit Consumer consent. Candidates are bounded by the published catalog, Consumer declaration and company approval, not the saved external scope snapshot. Consent permits client use; the Provider determines actual operation permissions. Scope changes do not pause grants. Permission failures affect the operation only; recovery does not require repeat Consumer consent. Genuine credential expiry or revocation still requires reconnect. Healthy accounts have no persistent permission-refresh button. Only server-indicated upgrade or reconnect states expose recovery actions; new Actions or external scope changes do not require account updates. New-capability notices exclude old unchecked catalog Actions. Never collect credentials in chat or silently grant new Actions.
